text: Supplied conformance is attributed as its own kind of component evidence (#279, #285). Each record names its exact production target, a selected conformance check and invocation, the runner and its pins, the actual outcome, the model's identity, the ratified bounds, whether it sampled or explored exhaustively, the runs, steps, states and transitions it observed, and its attempt coverage, kept apart. Its declarations and every execution input must match their snapshots. A record says only what its runs showed: a sampled run never establishes every state, nothing claims every step was tried without attempt coverage, and a failed attempt blocks the every-state claim while the transitions that passed stay recorded. All three kinds, proof, assumptions and conformance, replace and clear on their own and revalidate what the others retain, so a changed driver, model or bound can't hide behind an update to another kind. Nothing runs, and explicit component checks stay refused until adapters run them.
